chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Richard Davis and bowed bass
summary: Jackson praises Richard Davis's bowing that makes the bass sound like a cello.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: He could take a bow and make a bow play so -- he could take a bow just like, to me, the greatest guy I know today -- all due respects to you because you know I love you -- but, to me, I can listen to Richard Davis take a bow --
-- and make a bass fiddle sound like a cello.
I don't mean up in the upper range of the cello but the bass fiddle itself, its intonation, and his tone is so clear, you know.
To me he's another fantastic bass player.
You can almost say -- It's a shame to say this, Milt, but he almost plays too much.
There's no question. If a word could be applied properly, appropriately, you could say Richard Davis is super.
